extraction.body: This is CNBC's live coverage of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is stepping down as CEO of the chipmaker he co-founded 33 years ago and built into a $4 trillion company that powered the artificial intelligence boom, the company announced Thursday. CFO Colette Kress has been named interim CEO. "The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption," said board chair Harvey Jones in a release announcing the news. Kress also provided a statement in the release, but Huang was not quoted. After a meteoric rise to fame due to Nvidia's central role in AI, Huang's dramatic fall has been even more rapid, following a series of stinging revelations about his romantic ties to a woman believed by the U.S. intelligence community to be a Chinese spy. Huang, 63, apologized on Sunday for being "unfaithful to my wife," though he provided no details about the affair with businesswoman Alice Huang, who has worked for a Chinese company and Nvidia customer called Megaspeed. On Thursday, The New York Times reported that the Nvidia CEO also had a separate affair, this one with Kimberly Powell, vice president of health care at the chipmaker. Later that afternoon The Times and other outlets reported that Nvidia's board met to discuss the company's future. Jensen Huang denied allegations that he had compromised national security or Nvidia secrets after reports of the Alice Huang affair. The news sparked concerns that Nvidia knew companies based in Singapore and Malaysia had been evading U.S. export controls in accessing its technology. The board said on Tuesday that it had hired Wachtell Lipton to investigate the intelligence allegations. Huang's downfall also puts the spotlight on President Donald Trump , who formed a particularly close relationship with the CEO of what, until recently, was the world's most valuable company. Huang became a key voice on U.S. AI policy while pushing for issues that were in Nvidia's interest, such as preserving access to open-source AI, and lobbying to allow chip exports to China. In May, Huang joined Trump on a trip to China, and in August, while on stage at the All-In Summit to discuss AI safety and regulation, he took a call from Trump and put him on speakerphone. "I'm with you all the way," Trump told Huang and the audience. With Democrats poised to take over both houses of Congress and promising to investigate various matters related to Nvidia, Huang's status in Washington, D.C. was poised to change dramatically even before the affairs became public. Nvidia's fortunes exploded after OpenAI released ChatGPT in late 2022, leading to soaring demand for the chipmaker's graphics processing units, or GPUs. Nvidia's stock is up about 14-fold since then, even with a recent pullback related to the Huang scandal and the broader selloff in the AI trade. Beyond its impact on Nvidia, Huang's departure has deep ramifications for the AI industry that has turned Huang into a global spokesperson and celebrity, traversing the globe in his trademark leather jacket, touting the power of the advanced chips, models and agents. Huang has seeded the market with numerous companies that buy Nvidia GPUs, building his company's influence and establishing a deep roster of customers, beyond the hyperscalers. Nvidia has used its balance sheet to backstop leases and chip sales, and has become the centerpiece of the industry, acting as technology supplier, customer, investor, financier, and partner to scores of AI companies. "He's Mr. AI. He speaks for the industry," said Jeff Christian, CEO of Christian and Timbers, an executive search firm. "He's connected financially to everybody either through partnerships, or through lending the money to buy chips." Nvidia reiterated plans to announce third-quarter results on Nov. 17 despite the CEO transition. The company plans to post results around 1:20 p.m. PT and host an earnings call at 2 p.m. PT. Nvidia named Harvey C. Jones to serve as its "first-ever" board chair. He joined Nvidia's board in 1993, and is a former CEO and chairman of chip-design software maker Synopsys . Nvidia's new interim CEO Colette Kress joined the chipmaker in September 2013 and most recently served as executive vice president and finance chief. She previously worked for 13 years at Microsoft and as finance chief within Cisco's business tech and operations finance unit. She holds a finance degree from the University of Arizona and a master's in business administration from Southern Methodist University. The company said Kress will continue to serve as Executive Vice President and CFO while acting as interim CEO until a permanent successor has been named. "Jensen's contributions to NVIDIA are profound. NVIDIA is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry." Huang was born in Taiwan but grew up in the U.S. and is an American citizen. He founded Nvidia to make chips for computer graphics, both for video games and rendering. In the early 2000s, Huang and other executives saw an opportunity to allow scientists to use the company's GPUs to do computationally-intense work. That technology eventually allowed Nvidia's chips to transform from a leading player in video game technology to the most important player in AI and a key American asset for national defense.

Nvidia’s board of directors has confirmed today that Jensen Huang has resigned as the company's CEO. The news follows revelations that Huang had been involved in not one but two extramarital affairs, one with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset, and another with his direct report, Nvidia’s VP of health care, Kimberly Powell.

"NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) Board of Directors announced today that Jensen Huang has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately," the board stated. "Colette Kress, current Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of NVIDIA, has agreed to serve as Interim Chief Executive Officer. Kress will continue to serve as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer while serving as Interim Chief Executive Officer until a permanent successor has been named. The Board is initiating a search for a permanent Chief Executive Officer and will consider internal and external candidates."

In recent weeks, stories have come to light alleging that Huang was involved in an overly familiar relationship with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom U.S. intelligence agencies suspect may be a Chinese intelligence asset. It was reported that the AI GPU giant’s CEO may have been the target of a spy plot — Megaspeed is under investigatio n for its involvement in the smuggling of $2 billion worth of export-controlled AI GPUs into China.
Nvidia shares plunged more than 10 percent in early market trading following the news, and are now down more than 23% in the last month.

Over the weekend, Jensen Huang admitted that he had been unfaithful to his wife and issued a company-wide apology. Separately, Nvidia’s Board of Directors launched an independent investigation into reports that Huang’s entanglement may be a matter of national security , given his role in the global AI revolution.
Colette Kress has been Nvidia's Executive Vice President and CFO since September 2013; prior to that, she spent 25 years at Cisco and Microsoft , among others.

Just a couple of days later, a second bombshell report emerged claiming that Jensen Huang was also romantically involved with Powell , one of his direct reports at the company. Reports indicate the affair was known within the company, and that the two were even filmed being affectionate in a San Jose hotel at Nvidia GTC. Security allegedly sequestered a bystander who filmed the interaction on camera and made the person an offer to sign a nondisclosure agreement.

Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang has resigned following revelations that he had two extramarital affairs, plunging the chipmaker at the heart of the global AI boom into crisis. The 63-year-old will be replaced by chief financial officer Colette Kress, who will serve as interim chief executive. His exit comes after he admitted to having a relationship with a woman that US authorities believe was a Chinese spy. It also emerged on Wednesday that Huang had an affair with a senior Nvidia executive. Nvidia shares were down more than 10 percent in pre-market trading, extending earlier losses after the announcement of Huang’s resignation. Huang, who cofounded Nvidia in 1993, led it to become what was until recently the world’s most valuable company. Huang’s departure marks a startling end to his more than 33-year tenure, during which Nvidia evolved from a small video-game chip company into the linchpin of the global AI infrastructure boom. Huang has become one of the most recognizable figures in tech, as Nvidia’s semiconductors became integral to training and running AI systems such as OpenAI’s ChatGPT and Anthropic’s Claude. Nvidia stock extended its pre-market decline after the company announced that Jensen Huang had resigned as chief executive. Shares were down 10.2 percent in pre-market trading, a move that would wipe off more than $400 billion in market capitalization. extraction.body: This is CNBC's live coverage of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is stepping down as CEO of the chipmaker he co-founded 33 years ago and built into a $4 trillion company that powered the artificial intelligence boom, the company announced Thursday. CFO Colette Kress has been named interim CEO. "The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption," said board chair Harvey Jones in a release announcing the news. Kress also provided a statement in the release, but Huang was not quoted. After a meteoric rise to fame due to Nvidia's central role in AI, Huang's dramatic fall has been even more rapid, following a series of stinging revelations about his romantic ties to a woman believed by the U.S. intelligence community to be a Chinese spy. Huang, 63, apologized on Sunday for being "unfaithful to my wife," though he provided no details about the affair with businesswoman Alice Huang, who has worked for a Chinese company and Nvidia customer called Megaspeed. On Thursday, The New York Times reported that the Nvidia CEO also had a separate affair, this one with Kimberly Powell, vice president of health care at the chipmaker. Later that afternoon The Times and other outlets reported that Nvidia's board met to discuss the company's future. Jensen Huang denied allegations that he had compromised national security or Nvidia secrets after reports of the Alice Huang affair. The news sparked concerns that Nvidia knew companies based in Singapore and Malaysia had been evading U.S. export controls in accessing its technology. The board said on Tuesday that it had hired Wachtell Lipton to investigate the intelligence allegations. Huang's downfall also puts the spotlight on President Donald Trump , who formed a particularly close relationship with the CEO of what, until recently, was the world's most valuable company. Huang became a key voice on U.S. AI policy while pushing for issues that were in Nvidia's interest, such as preserving access to open-source AI, and lobbying to allow chip exports to China. In May, Huang joined Trump on a trip to China, and in August, while on stage at the All-In Summit to discuss AI safety and regulation, he took a call from Trump and put him on speakerphone. "I'm with you all the way," Trump told Huang and the audience. With Democrats poised to take over both houses of Congress and promising to investigate various matters related to Nvidia, Huang's status in Washington, D.C. was poised to change dramatically even before the affairs became public. Nvidia's fortunes exploded after OpenAI released ChatGPT in late 2022, leading to soaring demand for the chipmaker's graphics processing units, or GPUs. Nvidia's stock is up about 14-fold since then, even with a recent pullback related to the Huang scandal and the broader selloff in the AI trade. Beyond its impact on Nvidia, Huang's departure has deep ramifications for the AI industry that has turned Huang into a global spokesperson and celebrity, traversing the globe in his trademark leather jacket, touting the power of the advanced chips, models and agents. Huang has seeded the market with numerous companies that buy Nvidia GPUs, building his company's influence and establishing a deep roster of customers, beyond the hyperscalers. Nvidia has used its balance sheet to backstop leases and chip sales, and has become the centerpiece of the industry, acting as technology supplier, customer, investor, financier, and partner to scores of AI companies. "He's Mr. AI. He speaks for the industry," said Jeff Christian, CEO of Christian and Timbers, an executive search firm. "He's connected financially to everybody either through partnerships, or through lending the money to buy chips." Nvidia reiterated plans to announce third-quarter results on Nov. 17 despite the CEO transition. The company plans to post results around 1:20 p.m. PT and host an earnings call at 2 p.m. PT. Nvidia named Harvey C. Jones to serve as its "first-ever" board chair. He joined Nvidia's board in 1993, and is a former CEO and chairman of chip-design software maker Synopsys . Nvidia's new interim CEO Colette Kress joined the chipmaker in September 2013 and most recently served as executive vice president and finance chief. She previously worked for 13 years at Microsoft and as finance chief within Cisco's business tech and operations finance unit. She holds a finance degree from the University of Arizona and a master's in business administration from Southern Methodist University. The company said Kress will continue to serve as Executive Vice President and CFO while acting as interim CEO until a permanent successor has been named. "Jensen's contributions to NVIDIA are profound. NVIDIA is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry." Huang was born in Taiwan but grew up in the U.S. and is an American citizen. He founded Nvidia to make chips for computer graphics, both for video games and rendering. In the early 2000s, Huang and other executives saw an opportunity to allow scientists to use the company's GPUs to do computationally-intense work. That technology eventually allowed Nvidia's chips to transform from a leading player in video game technology to the most important player in AI and a key American asset for national defense.

Nvidia’s board of directors has confirmed today that Jensen Huang has resigned as the company's CEO. The news follows revelations that Huang had been involved in not one but two extramarital affairs, one with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset, and another with his direct report, Nvidia’s VP of health care, Kimberly Powell.

"NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) Board of Directors announced today that Jensen Huang has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately," the board stated. "Colette Kress, current Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of NVIDIA, has agreed to serve as Interim Chief Executive Officer. Kress will continue to serve as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer while serving as Interim Chief Executive Officer until a permanent successor has been named. The Board is initiating a search for a permanent Chief Executive Officer and will consider internal and external candidates."

In recent weeks, stories have come to light alleging that Huang was involved in an overly familiar relationship with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, whom U.S. intelligence agencies suspect may be a Chinese intelligence asset. It was reported that the AI GPU giant’s CEO may have been the target of a spy plot — Megaspeed is under investigatio n for its involvement in the smuggling of $2 billion worth of export-controlled AI GPUs into China.
Nvidia shares plunged more than 10 percent in early market trading following the news, and are now down more than 23% in the last month.

Over the weekend, Jensen Huang admitted that he had been unfaithful to his wife and issued a company-wide apology. Separately, Nvidia’s Board of Directors launched an independent investigation into reports that Huang’s entanglement may be a matter of national security , given his role in the global AI revolution.
Colette Kress has been Nvidia's Executive Vice President and CFO since September 2013; prior to that, she spent 25 years at Cisco and Microsoft , among others.

Just a couple of days later, a second bombshell report emerged claiming that Jensen Huang was also romantically involved with Powell , one of his direct reports at the company. Reports indicate the affair was known within the company, and that the two were even filmed being affectionate in a San Jose hotel at Nvidia GTC. Security allegedly sequestered a bystander who filmed the interaction on camera and made the person an offer to sign a nondisclosure agreement.

Nvidia also announced that Harvey C. Jones will serve as the company's first-ever Chair of the Board; he has previously served as CEO and Executive Chairman of Synopsys.

He has no obvious successor, and personally owns more than 870m shares, or about 3.6% of the company, making him the world’s 13th richest person according to Bloomberg. Unlike many of his contemporaries at other big tech companies, Huang has dozens of direct reports, an unusual management structure that emphasises his control over the company. The entire artificial intelligence ecosphere relies on the company, which engineers advanced chips used to train AI models and power companies such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Google. It is also one of the world’s most valuable companies, with a market cap of more than $4tn. Huang himself is one of the world’s richest people, with an estimated net worth of $148bn. US trade representative Jamieson ⁠Greer ⁠told CNBC on Thursday that ⁠the United States “remains ⁠concerned” ​about ‌the situation at Nvidia. Chiu Chui-cheng, Taiwan’s Mainland Affairs Council minister, said there were “no special flags” about her at the time, Chiu said, adding that “if we had any of the kind of critical intelligence … we would have definitely flagged her for heightened review”. Jensen Huang, who has been married to his wife, Lori, since 1985, admitted in an email to employees on Sunday that he had an affair and that he would cooperate with an internal investigation. Nvidia’s board of directors put out a statement the same day that the company was launching an investigation regarding reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. Donald Trump has backed Huang , saying he had done “an incredible job” and is “an honorable guy”. Leading tech industry players, including Elon Musk, have also thrown their support behind Huang. Musk was asked on X early on Thursday if he would hire a jobless Huang. He replied: “That would be an honour.” Democratic senators Elizabeth Warren ⁠and Chris Coons have asked the Trump administration to preserve all documents tied to Nvidia’s chip ⁠exports to China, it was revealed late on Wednesday. “This ‌incident raises significant ‌concerns about the federal government’s ability to effectively enforce our export ‌controls and protect our national security,” the senators said in the letter sent to the commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick; the secretary of state, Marco Rubio; and White House chief of staff, Stephen Miller. Nvidia did not immediately return a request for comment.

Shares of Nvidia fell in premarket as The Wall Street Journal reported that the company may soon remove CEO Jensen Huang. Investors are now trying to sort out what might come next, including possible replacement and downstream effects on other companies' shares. The Wall Street Journal reported late Wednesday that chip giant Nvidia (NVDA) was moving closer to doing something that a week ago seemed unthinkable: remove CEO Jensen Huang, who helped co-found the company in the 1990s and has led it since. That story landed along with another from The New York Times that said Huang had a relationship with a company executive; pressure on Huang followed reports that the company's board was investigating his relationship with another woman alleged to be a Chinese spy. Nvidia did not respond to Investopedia's requests for comment in time for publication. Shares of Nvidia, which had fallen nearly 10% this week through Tuesday's close, bounced during Wednesday's session but were recently down 8% in premarket action. The news was also affecting a range of other investments, with shares of some partners falling and select competitors moving higher. Speculation about replacements, including but not limited to current Nvidia executives, was also in full steam. Traders' perceived odds of Huang leaving the role were rising late Wednesday on prediction markets. On Kalshi, it was recently viewed as about 50/50 that he'd be out by Monday, while on Polymarket the odds of his departing being announced by the end of the year were above 75%. Nvidia's stock has been one of the stars of the bull run, with the company currently commanding the world's second-highest public valuation. That has lifted Huang's wealth and public profile, with the executive's net worth estimated by Forbes as above $150 billion. The latest developments come with the company scheduled to report third-quarter financial results next week. This article was first published on Nov. 11, 2026. It was updated to reflect new market data as of Thursday morning. sources.title: Nvidia’s stock drops as board reportedly preps to oust CEO Jensen Huang
passages: Nvidia is reportedly planning to oust its co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang, who has led the company for the last 33 years, the Wall Street Journal reports .
Sources told the newspaper that the Nvidia board is meeting as soon as Wednesday to determine Huang’s future at the company.
The stock is down about 11% in the past five days.
Huang famously delegates very little and has about 60 direct reports, he has said .
The company also has not had an obvious successor or a succession plan.
According to Bloomberg, Nvidia is working with an outside firm to identify candidates that could potentially replace Huang as CEO.

extraction.body: Jensen Huang , the high-flying founder and CEO of one of the most valuable companies in the world, resigned today following a meeting by Nvidia ‘s board of directors. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO as the giant chip maker looks for a permanent successor, the company said The AI chip-maker and its leader have been embroiled in controversy for the past few weeks. First as the news broke about his extramarital affair with a former Chinese state TV reporter turned data center exec, Alice Huang (no relation), for a company that is one of the Nvidia’s biggest customers in Southeast Asia. The New York Times then reported that U.S. intelligence officials believed that the data center exec was passing information on to the Chinese government. Today, the paper reported the Nvidia CEO also had an affair with an exec at his own company. Related Stories News Nvidia Becomes First $5 Trillion Company After Spree Of Product And Partnership News Festivals Infinity Festival's 8th Edition Slated For October At Sony Pictures Imageworks Mid-Wilshire Campus And Academy Museum The Times also reported that U.S. intelligence officials had made the White House aware of Huang’s involvement with a Chinese spy, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly briefing president Donald Trump, who considers Huang a friend. Trump said Monday and Huang denied knowing that Alice Huang had been collecting intelligence for Beijing. Watch on Deadline Jensen Huang cut a singular figure earning fame beyond the tech world for his Tom Ford leather jackets as well as his company’s dominance in the booming AI chip market. He appeared on the cover of the Time 100 issue of that same magazine in 2021. He and seven other industry CEOs graced the cover of the publication’s fabled “Person of the Year” issue. They were honored collectively as “the architects of AI.” Even after dropping down 10% in recent weeks amid the scandal, Nvidia was still valued at neearly 4.2 trillion at the end of trading on Wednesday. That makes it the second most valuable company in the world, trailing only Apple. Get our Breaking News Alerts and Keep your inbox happy. Comments On Deadline Hollywood are monitored. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will take over as interim CEO as the giant chip maker looks for a permanent successor, the company said

The AI chip-maker and its leader have been embroiled in controversy for the past few weeks. First as the news broke about his extramarital affair with a former Chinese state TV reporter turned data center exec, Alice Huang (no relation), for a company that is one of the Nvidia’s biggest customers in Southeast Asia. The New York Times then reported that U.S. intelligence officials believed that the data center exec was passing information on to the Chinese government. Today, the paper reported the Nvidia CEO also had an affair with an exec at his own company. Related Stories News Nvidia Becomes First $5 Trillion Company After Spree Of Product And Partnership News Festivals Infinity Festival's 8th Edition Slated For October At Sony Pictures Imageworks Mid-Wilshire Campus And Academy Museum

The Times also reported that U.S. intelligence officials had made the White House aware of Huang’s involvement with a Chinese spy, with Secretary of State Marco Rubio reportedly briefing president Donald Trump, who considers Huang a friend. Trump said Monday and Huang denied knowing that Alice Huang had been collecting intelligence for Beijing. Watch on Deadline

Jensen Huang cut a singular figure earning fame beyond the tech world for his Tom Ford leather jackets as well as his company’s dominance in the booming AI chip market. He appeared on the cover of the Time 100 issue of that same magazine in 2021. He and seven other industry CEOs graced the cover of the publication’s fabled “Person of the Year” issue. They were honored collectively as “the architects of AI.”

Even after dropping down 10% in recent weeks amid the scandal, Nvidia was still valued at neearly 4.2 trillion at the end of trading on Wednesday. That makes it the second most valuable company in the world, trailing only Apple.

extraction.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday after his extramarital affair raised national security concerns. The company named Colette Kress as interim CEO. She is the current executive vice president and chief financial officer. Huang faced growing calls to resign after his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Late Wednesday, media reports said Huang had another extramarital affair with an Nvidia employee who reports to him. The board of directors said Thursday it also named its first-ever chairman, Harvey C. Shares of Nvidia, one of the largest companies in the world, plunged 10% in premarket trading Thursday. Nvidia’s board had gathered to discuss Huang’s future after revelations that he was having an affair with a former Megaspeed executive suspected of being a Chinese government agent. The New York Times reported Wednesday that Huang also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reported to him. In its first statement since the scandal broke, Singapore-headquartered Megaspeed International said Thursday that it takes its obligation to comply with U.S. export control laws “extremely seriously.” Details about Huang’s affair with the former Megaspeed executive are unclear. “Megaspeed is committed to working constructively and transparently with the U.S. government,” said the statement signed by its chairman and CEO, Tan Yong Pong, who also goes by James Tan. Nvidia has said it had “no reason to believe” that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, but that its inquiry would examine all available information. The New York Times reported that the woman with whom Huang had an affair was Alice Huang, who also goes by the name Huang Le, and was a top executive at Megaspeed. The company prominently touts a partnership with Nvidia on its website. Last month, the Times reported that U.S. intelligence agencies discovered Nvidia’s Huang had developed a close relationship with Alice Huang — and determined she was feeding information directly to Beijing. President Donald Trump announced that the FBI was investigating. Megaspeed faced claims last year that it was illicitly shipping advanced Nvidia computer chips into China, but in December said there was “no evidence” of such exports. Singapore has also said it is investigating such allegations. China has denied that it engaged in an attempt to ensnare Huang, who heads one of the world’s most valuable companies. Nvidia has become a leader in making chips that power AI and Huang has lobbied Washington to loosen limits on sales of Nvidia chips to China. Megaspeed said Thursday that it has cooperated with the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS), which handles enforcement of national security restrictions on exports of technology, and was ready to “cooperate fully with any other relevant U.S. government authority.” It said it has hired a U.S. law firm to handle a “comprehensive census” of its computer chips and to verify its export controls. “Megaspeed welcomes appropriate government scrutiny and is committed to demonstrating through concrete actions that it operates responsibly, transparently, and in accordance with applicable U.S. laws,” it said. Apart from questions over national security, Megaspeed’s finances also have drawn attention. Its total assets soared roughly 90-fold from late 2023 to 2024, to almost US$3 billion, according to Singapore corporate records. Revenue surged to over US$294 million in 2024 from none in 2023.

extraction.body: This is CNBC's live coverage of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is stepping down as CEO of the chipmaker he co-founded 33 years ago and built into a $4 trillion company that powered the artificial intelligence boom, the company announced Thursday. CFO Colette Kress has been named interim CEO. "The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption," said board chair Harvey Jones in a release announcing the news. Kress also provided a statement in the release, but Huang was not quoted. After a meteoric rise to fame due to Nvidia's central role in AI, Huang's dramatic fall has been even more rapid, following a series of stinging revelations about his romantic ties to a woman believed by the U.S. intelligence community to be a Chinese spy. Huang, 63, apologized on Sunday for being "unfaithful to my wife," though he provided no details about the affair with businesswoman Alice Huang, who has worked for a Chinese company and Nvidia customer called Megaspeed. On Thursday, The New York Times reported that the Nvidia CEO also had a separate affair, this one with Kimberly Powell, vice president of health care at the chipmaker. Later that afternoon The Times and other outlets reported that Nvidia's board met to discuss the company's future. Jensen Huang denied allegations that he had compromised national security or Nvidia secrets after reports of the Alice Huang affair. The news sparked concerns that Nvidia knew companies based in Singapore and Malaysia had been evading U.S. export controls in accessing its technology. The board said on Tuesday that it had hired Wachtell Lipton to investigate the intelligence allegations. Huang's downfall also puts the spotlight on President Donald Trump , who formed a particularly close relationship with the CEO of what, until recently, was the world's most valuable company. Huang became a key voice on U.S. AI policy while pushing for issues that were in Nvidia's interest, such as preserving access to open-source AI, and lobbying to allow chip exports to China. In May, Huang joined Trump on a trip to China, and in August, while on stage at the All-In Summit to discuss AI safety and regulation, he took a call from Trump and put him on speakerphone. "I'm with you all the way," Trump told Huang and the audience. With Democrats poised to take over both houses of Congress and promising to investigate various matters related to Nvidia, Huang's status in Washington, D.C. was poised to change dramatically even before the affairs became public. Nvidia's fortunes exploded after OpenAI released ChatGPT in late 2022, leading to soaring demand for the chipmaker's graphics processing units, or GPUs. Nvidia's stock is up about 14-fold since then, even with a recent pullback related to the Huang scandal and the broader selloff in the AI trade. Beyond its impact on Nvidia, Huang's departure has deep ramifications for the AI industry that has turned Huang into a global spokesperson and celebrity, traversing the globe in his trademark leather jacket, touting the power of the advanced chips, models and agents. Huang has seeded the market with numerous companies that buy Nvidia GPUs, building his company's influence and establishing a deep roster of customers, beyond the hyperscalers. Nvidia has used its balance sheet to backstop leases and chip sales, and has become the centerpiece of the industry, acting as technology supplier, customer, investor, financier, and partner to scores of AI companies. "He's Mr. AI. He speaks for the industry," said Jeff Christian, CEO of Christian and Timbers, an executive search firm. "He's connected financially to everybody either through partnerships, or through lending the money to buy chips." Nvidia reiterated plans to announce third-quarter results on Nov. 17 despite the CEO transition. The company plans to post results around 1:20 p.m. PT and host an earnings call at 2 p.m. PT. Nvidia named Harvey C. Jones to serve as its "first-ever" board chair. He joined Nvidia's board in 1993, and is a former CEO and chairman of chip-design software maker Synopsys . Nvidia's new interim CEO Colette Kress joined the chipmaker in September 2013 and most recently served as executive vice president and finance chief. She previously worked for 13 years at Microsoft and as finance chief within Cisco's business tech and operations finance unit. She holds a finance degree from the University of Arizona and a master's in business administration from Southern Methodist University. The company said Kress will continue to serve as Executive Vice President and CFO while acting as interim CEO until a permanent successor has been named. "Jensen's contributions to NVIDIA are profound. NVIDIA is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry." Huang was born in Taiwan but grew up in the U.S. and is an American citizen. He founded Nvidia to make chips for computer graphics, both for video games and rendering. In the early 2000s, Huang and other executives saw an opportunity to allow scientists to use the company's GPUs to do computationally-intense work. That technology eventually allowed Nvidia's chips to transform from a leading player in video game technology to the most important player in AI and a key American asset for national defense. His fame in Taiwan is so great than when he returns home, "Jensanity" surrounds him.

extraction.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday after his extramarital affair raised national security concerns. The company named Colette Kress as interim CEO. She is the current executive vice president and chief financial officer. Huang faced growing calls to resign after his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Late Wednesday, media reports said Huang had another extramarital affair with an Nvidia employee who reports to him. The board of directors said Thursday it also named its first-ever chairman, Harvey C. Shares of Nvidia, one of the largest companies in the world, plunged 10% in premarket trading Thursday. Nvidia’s board had gathered to discuss Huang’s future after revelations that he was having an affair with a former Megaspeed executive suspected of being a Chinese government agent. The New York Times reported Wednesday that Huang also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reported to him. In its first statement since the scandal broke, Singapore-headquartered Megaspeed International said Thursday that it takes its obligation to comply with U.S. export control laws “extremely seriously.” Details about Huang’s affair with the former Megaspeed executive are unclear. “Megaspeed is committed to working constructively and transparently with the U.S. government,” said the statement signed by its chairman and CEO, Tan Yong Pong, who also goes by James Tan. Nvidia has said it had “no reason to believe” that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, but that its inquiry would examine all available information. The New York Times reported that the woman with whom Huang had an affair was Alice Huang, who also goes by the name Huang Le, and was a top executive at Megaspeed. The company prominently touts a partnership with Nvidia on its website. Last month, the Times reported that U.S. intelligence agencies discovered Nvidia’s Huang had developed a close relationship with Alice Huang — and determined she was feeding information directly to Beijing. President Donald Trump announced that the FBI was investigating. Megaspeed faced claims last year that it was illicitly shipping advanced Nvidia computer chips into China, but in December said there was “no evidence” of such exports. Singapore has also said it is investigating such allegations. China has denied that it engaged in an attempt to ensnare Huang, who heads one of the world’s most valuable companies. Nvidia has become a leader in making chips that power AI and Huang has lobbied Washington to loosen limits on sales of Nvidia chips to China. Megaspeed said Thursday that it has cooperated with the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS), which handles enforcement of national security restrictions on exports of technology, and was ready to “cooperate fully with any other relevant U.S. government authority.” It said it has hired a U.S. law firm to handle a “comprehensive census” of its computer chips and to verify its export controls. “Megaspeed welcomes appropriate government scrutiny and is committed to demonstrating through concrete actions that it operates responsibly, transparently, and in accordance with applicable U.S. laws,” it said. Apart from questions over national security, Megaspeed’s finances also have drawn attention. Its total assets soared roughly 90-fold from late 2023 to 2024, to almost US$3 billion, according to Singapore corporate records. Revenue surged to over US$294 million in 2024 from none in 2023.

extraction.body: Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of tech giant Nvidia, the company's board says Stocks in the firm plummeted again after the New York Times reported that Huang had a second affair with an executive at his own company US markets will open again at 14:30 GMT (09:30 ET), with pre-market trading showing Nvidia's shares down 10% Edited by Jamie Whitehead and Ben Hatton, with reporting by technology editor Zoe Kleinman Colette Kress, who has just been made the interim CEO of Nvidia, says that she is committed to building on the "the extraordinary foundation" that Jensen Huang has created. Kress has been the executive vice president and chief financial officer at Nvidia since joining the company in September 2013. Before joining Nvidia, Kress spent nearly 25 years in finance roles at leading technology companies, including Cisco and Microsoft. After being appointed as interim chief executive officer, Kress says: "Nvidia's strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years. "We will continue advancing the work that has made Nvidia a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders." Nvidia shares are down more than 10% in pre-market trading, and all eyes will be on the company’s share price as the market opens at 09:30 ET (14:30 GMT) following the news Jensen Huang has resigned. The rolling news of his alleged affairs has affected the firm’s share price for most of the week as investors have fretted over who could run the company should Huang leave. Britzman also expects some "short-term turbulence" for Nvidia, but says "demand for AI isn't going anywhere". On The Global Story, host Asma Khalid speaks to Randy Schriver and Mike Kuiken of the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission about the national security implications and what the Nvidia scandal could mean for America’s approach to selling advanced chips to China. BBC economics editor Faisal Islam also offers a behind-the-scenes look at Jensen Huang, the man at the centre of it all, and his extraordinary influence over the global AI race. Jensen Huang's position as CEO of Nvidia hangs in the balance after reports of two affairs, one of which may have been with an alleged Chinese spy. Who is Jensen Huang? Born in Taiwan, Huang, 63, co-founded the US tech giant Nvidia in 1993 and has led it to become a multi-trillion-dollar company. He has been dubbed the "Taylor Swift of tech" and has an estimated net worth of $145bn (£109bn). What is Nvidia? It's a leading provider of advanced computer chips, which are critical to technologies including video games, cloud servers and, most importantly, AI. Worth more than $4tn, Nvidia is the world's second-most valuable company . The two reported affairs: Huang is reported to have had an extramarital affair with alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang. He admitted to being unfaithful in an apology email to Nvidia employees, but didn't name the woman involved. A second alleged affair with an employee has been reported by the New York Times . The impact: Nvidia shares have plunged, down almost 7.5% in after-hours trading. The company has launched an investigation into the scandal, and the board is reportedly meeting to decide Huang's future . After reports emerged that Nvidia boss and co-founder Jensen Huang allegedly had a second extramarital affair and there is now speculation about his future at the firm, the company’s share price plunged a further 8% in after-hours trading on Wall Street. If Nvidia’s shares open at the overnight price, they’ll have fallen from just over $188 each at close of play on Friday - before the company’s weekend announcement , external - to $158. The company’s market value would tumble from $4.5 trillion to $3.8 trillion. Our colleagues at BBC Newsday have been speaking to Michael Kovrig - a former Canadian diplomat who was held in China for more than 1,000 days in what was seen as a retaliatory act by the Chinese government. On Jensen Huang's alleged affair with Alice Huang, who is linked to a Singaporean company and was reportedly a Chinese spy, Kovrig says there were "probably actually two things going on". The first, he says, is that Alice Huang was possibly "some kind of 'white glove' - or someone that is fronting for other commercial entities in China that were trying to acquire these [Nvidia] chips". As a reminder, we haven't heard from Alice Huang since the allegations emerged - she is reportedly now in Beijing. Earlier today, her former company in Singapore, Megaspeed , said it was "committed to working constructively and transparently with the US government". On Sunday, Jensen Huang admitted having an affair - although he did not say with whom. Since then, reports of a second affair , with a woman at his own company, have emerged. Former US secretary of state Antony Blinken (R), former Canadian foreign minister Melanie Joy (M) and Michael Kovrig pictured in 2023 Separate from the affair with alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has been accused of having a second affair with an executive at his company. This was first reported by the New York Times , external , which said it had spoken to five people who had worked at Nvidia on condition of anonymity. Sources also said that the relationship between Huang and the woman had been discussed inside the company. The New York Times said that when it called Huang on Wednesday to ask about his alleged second affair, the CEO replied "I don’t think you should be talking to me directly," and hung up. Megaspeed, the Singaporean company associated with suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang, has issued a statement days after Nvidia launched an investigation into Jensen Huang’s affair earlier this week . Its chief executive, Tan Yong Pong, also known as James Tan, said the company "takes its compliance obligations under US export control laws extremely seriously" and is "committed to working constructively and transparently with the US government". At the heart of lawmakers’ concerns is whether sensitive US technology or information was put at risk. Colette Kress, who has just been made the interim CEO of Nvidia, says that she is committed to building on the "the extraordinary foundation" that Jensen Huang has created.
Kress has been the executive vice president and chief financial officer at Nvidia since joining the company in September 2013.
Before joining Nvidia, Kress spent nearly 25 years in finance roles at leading technology companies, including Cisco and Microsoft.

After being appointed as interim chief executive officer, Kress says: "Nvidia's strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years.

"We will continue advancing the work that has made Nvidia a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders."
Nvidia shares are down more than 10% in pre-market trading, and all eyes will be on the company’s share price as the market opens at 09:30 ET (14:30 GMT) following the news Jensen Huang has resigned.
The rolling news of his alleged affairs has affected the firm’s share price for most of the week as investors have fretted over who could run the company should Huang leave.
Britzman also expects some "short-term turbulence" for Nvidia, but says "demand for AI isn't going anywhere".

Jensen Huang's position as CEO of Nvidia hangs in the balance after reports of two affairs, one of which may have been with an alleged Chinese spy.

Who is Jensen Huang? Born in Taiwan, Huang, 63, co-founded the US tech giant Nvidia in 1993 and has led it to become a multi-trillion-dollar company. He has been dubbed the "Taylor Swift of tech" and has an estimated net worth of $145bn (£109bn).

What is Nvidia? It's a leading provider of advanced computer chips, which are critical to technologies including video games, cloud servers and, most importantly, AI. Worth more than $4tn, Nvidia is the world's second-most valuable company .

The two reported affairs: Huang is reported to have had an extramarital affair with alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang. He admitted to being unfaithful in an apology email to Nvidia employees, but didn't name the woman involved. A second alleged affair with an employee has been reported by the New York Times .

After reports emerged that Nvidia boss and co-founder Jensen Huang allegedly had a second extramarital affair and there is now speculation about his future at the firm, the company’s share price plunged a further 8% in after-hours trading on Wall Street.

If Nvidia’s shares open at the overnight price, they’ll have fallen from just over $188 each at close of play on Friday - before the company’s weekend announcement , external - to $158. The company’s market value would tumble from $4.5 trillion to $3.8 trillion.

Our colleagues at BBC Newsday have been speaking to Michael Kovrig - a former Canadian diplomat who was held in China for more than 1,000 days in what was seen as a retaliatory act by the Chinese government.
On Jensen Huang's alleged affair with Alice Huang, who is linked to a Singaporean company and was reportedly a Chinese spy, Kovrig says there were "probably actually two things going on".

The first, he says, is that Alice Huang was possibly "some kind of 'white glove' - or someone that is fronting for other commercial entities in China that were trying to acquire these [Nvidia] chips".

As a reminder, we haven't heard from Alice Huang since the allegations emerged - she is reportedly now in Beijing. Earlier today, her former company in Singapore, Megaspeed , said it was "committed to working constructively and transparently with the US government".
On Sunday, Jensen Huang admitted having an affair - although he did not say with whom. Since then, reports of a second affair , with a woman at his own company, have emerged.

Separate from the affair with alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has been accused of having a second affair with an executive at his company.
This was first reported by the New York Times , external , which said it had spoken to five people who had worked at Nvidia on condition of anonymity.
Sources also said that the relationship between Huang and the woman had been discussed inside the company.
The New York Times said that when it called Huang on Wednesday to ask about his alleged second affair, the CEO replied "I don’t think you should be talking to me directly," and hung up.
Megaspeed, the Singaporean company associated with suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang, has issued a statement days after Nvidia launched an investigation into Jensen Huang’s affair earlier this week .

Its chief executive, Tan Yong Pong, also known as James Tan, said the company "takes its compliance obligations under US export control laws extremely seriously" and is "committed to working constructively and transparently with the US government".
At the heart of lawmakers’ concerns is whether sensitive US technology or information was put at risk.
When it announced its investigation on Sunday, Nvidia’s board said it had no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised - but that was before today’s developments.

extraction.body: This is CNBC's live coverage of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is stepping down as CEO of the chipmaker he co-founded 33 years ago and built into a $4 trillion company that powered the artificial intelligence boom, the company announced Thursday. CFO Colette Kress has been named interim CEO. "The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption," said board chair Harvey Jones in a release announcing the news. Kress also provided a statement in the release, but Huang was not quoted. After a meteoric rise to fame due to Nvidia's central role in AI, Huang's dramatic fall has been even more rapid, following a series of stinging revelations about his romantic ties to a woman believed by the U.S. intelligence community to be a Chinese spy. Huang, 63, apologized on Sunday for being "unfaithful to my wife," though he provided no details about the affair with businesswoman Alice Huang, who has worked for a Chinese company and Nvidia customer called Megaspeed. On Thursday, The New York Times reported that the Nvidia CEO also had a separate affair, this one with Kimberly Powell, vice president of health care at the chipmaker. Later that afternoon The Times and other outlets reported that Nvidia's board met to discuss the company's future. Jensen Huang denied allegations that he had compromised national security or Nvidia secrets after reports of the Alice Huang affair. The news sparked concerns that Nvidia knew companies based in Singapore and Malaysia had been evading U.S. export controls in accessing its technology. The board said on Tuesday that it had hired Wachtell Lipton to investigate the intelligence allegations. Huang's downfall also puts the spotlight on President Donald Trump , who formed a particularly close relationship with the CEO of what, until recently, was the world's most valuable company. Huang became a key voice on U.S. AI policy while pushing for issues that were in Nvidia's interest, such as preserving access to open-source AI, and lobbying to allow chip exports to China. In May, Huang joined Trump on a trip to China, and in August, while on stage at the All-In Summit to discuss AI safety and regulation, he took a call from Trump and put him on speakerphone. "I'm with you all the way," Trump told Huang and the audience. With Democrats poised to take over both houses of Congress and promising to investigate various matters related to Nvidia, Huang's status in Washington, D.C. was poised to change dramatically even before the affairs became public. Nvidia's fortunes exploded after OpenAI released ChatGPT in late 2022, leading to soaring demand for the chipmaker's graphics processing units, or GPUs. Nvidia's stock is up about 14-fold since then, even with a recent pullback related to the Huang scandal and the broader selloff in the AI trade. Beyond its impact on Nvidia, Huang's departure has deep ramifications for the AI industry that has turned Huang into a global spokesperson and celebrity, traversing the globe in his trademark leather jacket, touting the power of the advanced chips, models and agents. Huang has seeded the market with numerous companies that buy Nvidia GPUs, building his company's influence and establishing a deep roster of customers, beyond the hyperscalers. Nvidia has used its balance sheet to backstop leases and chip sales, and has become the centerpiece of the industry, acting as technology supplier, customer, investor, financier, and partner to scores of AI companies. "He's Mr. AI. He speaks for the industry," said Jeff Christian, CEO of Christian and Timbers, an executive search firm. "He's connected financially to everybody either through partnerships, or through lending the money to buy chips." Nvidia reiterated plans to announce third-quarter results on Nov. 17 despite the CEO transition. The company plans to post results around 1:20 p.m. PT and host an earnings call at 2 p.m. PT. Nvidia named Harvey C. Jones to serve as its "first-ever" board chair. He joined Nvidia's board in 1993, and is a former CEO and chairman of chip-design software maker Synopsys . Nvidia's new interim CEO Colette Kress joined the chipmaker in September 2013 and most recently served as executive vice president and finance chief. She previously worked for 13 years at Microsoft and as finance chief within Cisco's business tech and operations finance unit. She holds a finance degree from the University of Arizona and a master's in business administration from Southern Methodist University. The company said Kress will continue to serve as Executive Vice President and CFO while acting as interim CEO until a permanent successor has been named. "Jensen's contributions to NVIDIA are profound. NVIDIA is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry." Huang was born in Taiwan but grew up in the U.S. and is an American citizen. He founded Nvidia to make chips for computer graphics, both for video games and rendering. In the early 2000s, Huang and other executives saw an opportunity to allow scientists to use the company's GPUs to do computationally-intense work. That technology eventually allowed Nvidia's chips to transform from a leading player in video game technology to the most important player in AI and a key American asset for national defense. His fame in Taiwan is so great than when he returns home, "Jensanity" surrounds him.

If confirmed, the allegations could add a new corporate-governance problem to the company's existing leadership controversy. Nvidia (NVDA) shares are falling sharply in after-hours trading following a new report from The New York Times alleging that CEO Jensen Huang had a relationship with a company executive who reports to him. According to a market quote captured at 00:11 GMT+2 on November 12, NVDA traded at $167.37 after hours, down $6.36 or 3.66% from Wednesday's regular-session close of $173.73. The decline reverses more than Wednesday's 2.87% regular-session gain. The New York Times reported the new allegation late Wednesday, adding another potential complication for Nvidia's board of directors. The company is already investigating Huang following earlier reports concerning his relationship with a Chinese businesswoman whom U.S. intelligence reportedly identified as having connections to Chinese intelligence. That earlier controversy raised questions about national security, corporate oversight and whether sensitive information could have been compromised. The latest allegation, however, introduces a potentially different concern. If Huang had a relationship with an executive who reported directly to him, investors could reasonably question whether there were conflicts of interest involving management decisions, compensation, promotions or internal corporate governance. A personal relationship does not, by itself, establish wrongdoing or improper conduct. The significance depends on the circumstances, the company's policies, what was disclosed to the board and whether any business decisions were affected. The new allegation has not been independently verified by investingLive. Jensen Huang is not an ordinary corporate CEO. He co-founded Nvidia and has been central to its transformation into one of the world's most important artificial intelligence companies. For shareholders, the concern is not simply the executive's personal conduct. It is whether repeated controversies could undermine confidence in Nvidia's leadership, distract management or increase pressure on its board. There are three particularly important implications. Corporate governance: Investors may demand clearer answers about how Nvidia's board oversees its CEO and manages potential conflicts of interest. Leadership continuity: Any widening of the investigation could raise further questions about succession planning at a company closely associated with its founder. Valuation and investor confidence: Even without changes to Nvidia's chip demand, earnings or competitive position, greater uncertainty about leadership could influence how much investors are willing to pay for the stock. That does not mean Huang will leave Nvidia or that the allegations will ultimately affect the company's operations. But investors may increasingly distinguish between confidence in Nvidia's AI business and confidence in its corporate leadership. The immediate question is whether the after-hours selling continues when regular U.S. trading resumes Thursday, November 12. The reported decline comes while the Nasdaq futures market is closed, limiting the ability to draw conclusions about the broader technology sector's reaction at that moment. Traders should monitor whether Nvidia underperforms the Nasdaq and semiconductor stocks once futures trading resumes, and whether the company or its board responds to the latest reporting. A recovery toward Wednesday's $173.73 closing price would suggest the initial selling is being absorbed. Sustained weakness would raise the possibility that investors are assigning a greater risk premium to Nvidia's leadership uncertainty. For now, the market is reacting to another allegation rather than a confirmed finding of misconduct. What matters next is the evidence, the board's response and whether the situation begins to affect the company's ability to operate under its existing leadership. The decline reverses more than Wednesday's 2.87% regular-session gain. The New York Times reported the new allegation late Wednesday, adding another potential complication for Nvidia's board of directors. The company is already investigating Huang following earlier reports concerning his relationship with a Chinese businesswoman whom U.S. intelligence reportedly identified as having connections to Chinese intelligence. That earlier controversy raised questions about national security, corporate oversight and whether sensitive information could have been compromised. The latest allegation, however, introduces a potentially different concern. If Huang had a relationship with an executive who reported directly to him, investors could reasonably question whether there were conflicts of interest involving management decisions, compensation, promotions or internal corporate governance. A personal relationship does not, by itself, establish wrongdoing or improper conduct. The significance depends on the circumstances, the company's policies, what was disclosed to the board and whether any business decisions were affected. It is whether repeated controversies could undermine confidence in Nvidia's leadership, distract management or increase pressure on its board. There are three particularly important implications. Corporate governance: Investors may demand clearer answers about how Nvidia's board oversees its CEO and manages potential conflicts of interest. Leadership continuity: Any widening of the investigation could raise further questions about succession planning at a company closely associated with its founder. extraction.body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday after his extramarital affair raised national security concerns. The company named Colette Kress as interim CEO. She is the current executive vice president and chief financial officer. Huang faced growing calls to resign after his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Late Wednesday, media reports said Huang had another extramarital affair with an Nvidia employee who reports to him. The board of directors said Thursday it also named its first-ever chairman, Harvey C. Shares of Nvidia, one of the largest companies in the world, plunged 10% in premarket trading Thursday. Nvidia’s board had gathered to discuss Huang’s future after revelations that he was having an affair with a former Megaspeed executive suspected of being a Chinese government agent. The New York Times reported Wednesday that Huang also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reported to him. In its first statement since the scandal broke, Singapore-headquartered Megaspeed International said Thursday that it takes its obligation to comply with U.S. export control laws “extremely seriously.” Details about Huang’s affair with the former Megaspeed executive are unclear. “Megaspeed is committed to working constructively and transparently with the U.S. government,” said the statement signed by its chairman and CEO, Tan Yong Pong, who also goes by James Tan. Nvidia has said it had “no reason to believe” that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, but that its inquiry would examine all available information. The New York Times reported that the woman with whom Huang had an affair was Alice Huang, who also goes by the name Huang Le, and was a top executive at Megaspeed. The company prominently touts a partnership with Nvidia on its website. Last month, the Times reported that U.S. intelligence agencies discovered Nvidia’s Huang had developed a close relationship with Alice Huang — and determined she was feeding information directly to Beijing. President Donald Trump announced that the FBI was investigating. Megaspeed faced claims last year that it was illicitly shipping advanced Nvidia computer chips into China, but in December said there was “no evidence” of such exports. Singapore has also said it is investigating such allegations. China has denied that it engaged in an attempt to ensnare Huang, who heads one of the world’s most valuable companies. Nvidia has become a leader in making chips that power AI and Huang has lobbied Washington to loosen limits on sales of Nvidia chips to China. Megaspeed said Thursday that it has cooperated with the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS), which handles enforcement of national security restrictions on exports of technology, and was ready to “cooperate fully with any other relevant U.S. government authority.” It said it has hired a U.S. law firm to handle a “comprehensive census” of its computer chips and to verify its export controls. “Megaspeed welcomes appropriate government scrutiny and is committed to demonstrating through concrete actions that it operates responsibly, transparently, and in accordance with applicable U.S. laws,” it said. Apart from questions over national security, Megaspeed’s finances also have drawn attention. Its total assets soared roughly 90-fold from late 2023 to 2024, to almost US$3 billion, according to Singapore corporate records. Revenue surged to over US$294 million in 2024 from none in 2023.

extraction.body: Nvidia’s board announced that Jensen Huang — its longtime co-founder, president, and CEO — has resigned after reports of two extramarital affairs, one with an alleged Chinese spy and one with an Nvidia executive who reported to Huang. A press release published Thursday following a late Wednesday night board meeting announced Huang’s resignation as CEO, president, and board member, effective immediately, with current CFO Colette Kress appointed interim CEO. Kress has been with Nvidia since 2013, with previous stops at Cisco and Microsoft. Nvidia is also changing its corporate structure in Huang’s absence, appointing former Synopsys CEO Harvey C. The statement does not include a quote from Huang, while Kress is quoted as saying, “NVIDIA’s strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years. We will continue advancing the work that has made NVIDIA a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders.” Now Nvidia says, “The Board is initiating a search for a permanent Chief Executive Officer and will consider internal and external candidates,” and reports about who that might be have already surfaced, putting Kress, Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji, Nvidia VP Ian Buck, AMD CEO (and cousin of Jensen Huang) Lisa Su, and Arm CEO Rene Haas at the top of the list. Huang had been at the helm of what’s now known as the most powerful company in AI since its founding in 1993. In the years since, it’s become the main purveyor of the chips fueling AI advancement and deployment in the US, and it has enjoyed near-unbridled power and influence — demand for Nvidia’s chips constantly outpaces supply, and AI CEOs are constantly putting in requests to buy more, sometimes to no avail. Nvidia’s investment portfolio — worth about $99 billion and spanning AI companies from frontier labs to neoclouds — has also granted it a lot of sway in the AI space. And in recent years, Huang himself has enjoyed a close relationship with President Donald Trump. Over the past week, that influence has been a double-edged sword for Huang, after news broke that he had been involved in a romantic relationship with Alice Huang (no relation), an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud provider and big customer of Nvidia itself. The Megaspeed executive was also allegedly a surveillance operative passing information along to China’s Ministry of State Security. She was focused on gaining information about advanced AI chips in the US and trying to influence the technology being made available to China, The New York Times reported. Huang admitted he had been “unfaithful” to his wife and apologized to his family and shareholders in a memo to Nvidia employees over the weekend. As The Verge wrote earlier this week, “questions are swirling around how the affair may have influenced Huang’s reported push to sell advanced chips to China — and potentially even influenced President Trump’s own decisions surrounding AI export controls.” As of Monday, analysts, venture capitalists and even Trump had expected Huang would come out the other side of the scandal with his chief executive status intact. Silicon Valley insiders, including Elon Musk, had backed him despite the news. But on Wednesday, news broke that Huang had had a second extramarital affair — this time with an executive reporting directly to him. The New York Times, citing five people who worked at Nvidia, identified the relationship as being with Nvidia’s VP of healthcare, Kimberly Powell. Soon after the news broke, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the matter, that Nvidia’s board was meeting as soon as Wednesday evening in order to decide Huang’s future at the company and potentially oust him from his role.

extraction.body: Nvidia’s board announced that Jensen Huang — its longtime co-founder, president, and CEO — has resigned after reports of two extramarital affairs, one with an alleged Chinese spy and one with an Nvidia executive who reported to Huang. A press release published Thursday following a late Wednesday night board meeting announced Huang’s resignation as CEO, president, and board member, effective immediately, with current CFO Colette Kress appointed interim CEO. Kress has been with Nvidia since 2013, with previous stops at Cisco and Microsoft. Nvidia is also changing its corporate structure in Huang’s absence, appointing former Synopsys CEO Harvey C. The statement does not include a quote from Huang, while Kress is quoted as saying, “NVIDIA’s strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years. We will continue advancing the work that has made NVIDIA a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders.” Now Nvidia says, “The Board is initiating a search for a permanent Chief Executive Officer and will consider internal and external candidates,” and reports about who that might be have already surfaced, putting Kress, Apple hardware chief Johny Srouji, Nvidia VP Ian Buck, AMD CEO (and cousin of Jensen Huang) Lisa Su, and Arm CEO Rene Haas at the top of the list. Huang had been at the helm of what’s now known as the most powerful company in AI since its founding in 1993. In the years since, it’s become the main purveyor of the chips fueling AI advancement and deployment in the US, and it has enjoyed near-unbridled power and influence — demand for Nvidia’s chips constantly outpaces supply, and AI CEOs are constantly putting in requests to buy more, sometimes to no avail. Nvidia’s investment portfolio — worth about $99 billion and spanning AI companies from frontier labs to neoclouds — has also granted it a lot of sway in the AI space. And in recent years, Huang himself has enjoyed a close relationship with President Donald Trump. Over the past week, that influence has been a double-edged sword for Huang, after news broke that he had been involved in a romantic relationship with Alice Huang (no relation), an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based cloud provider and big customer of Nvidia itself. The Megaspeed executive was also allegedly a surveillance operative passing information along to China’s Ministry of State Security. She was focused on gaining information about advanced AI chips in the US and trying to influence the technology being made available to China, The New York Times reported. Huang admitted he had been “unfaithful” to his wife and apologized to his family and shareholders in a memo to Nvidia employees over the weekend. As The Verge wrote earlier this week, “questions are swirling around how the affair may have influenced Huang’s reported push to sell advanced chips to China — and potentially even influenced President Trump’s own decisions surrounding AI export controls.” As of Monday, analysts, venture capitalists and even Trump had expected Huang would come out the other side of the scandal with his chief executive status intact. Silicon Valley insiders, including Elon Musk, had backed him despite the news. But on Wednesday, news broke that Huang had had a second extramarital affair — this time with an executive reporting directly to him. The New York Times, citing five people who worked at Nvidia, identified the relationship as being with Nvidia’s VP of healthcare, Kimberly Powell. Soon after the news broke, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the matter, that Nvidia’s board was meeting as soon as Wednesday evening in order to decide Huang’s future at the company and potentially oust him from his role.

Last week, Mast as well as Rick Crawford, the chair of the House Intelligence Committee, and John Moolenaar, the chair of the House China Committee, sent Huang a letter requesting he appear for a "joint, closed-door briefing." Jensen Huang has not yet responded to the Republicans' request that he appear for a briefing. Asked by ABC News if he would consider issuing a subpoena to Huang should he not respond, Mast said "absolutely." It's unclear how a potential subpoena of Huang would play out. House Republicans lose control of their committees in January when the chamber turns over to Democrats. The subpoena would likely expire and Democrats would need to issue a new one. ABC News reached out to Nvidia for comment from Huang for this story. Congressional Republicans on the Select Committee on China also sent a letter to Huang requesting that he appear for a closed-door briefing Nov. 18 concerning his relationship with Alice Huang. It is not known if Huang will appear before that committee; Nvidia hasn't publicly responded to the request. Mast said there is a "lengthy" list of things he wants to hear from the Nvidia CEO including what correspondence he had with the Chinese government. Mast added that he is "100%" worried about the national security implications of Huang's reported relationship given that he runs the world's largest computer chip manufacturer. "They're American chips. You know. So we thank God that Jensen is an American entrepreneur. You know, it's an American tech company because they're the best chips anywhere in the globe," Mast said. "But that being said, we don't want China to access them, to use them, to produce them like that." Nvidia's board said they have "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised" by Huang's affair. Huang "fully supports the review" and will cooperate with it, the Nvidia statement further said. "We're going to need a full briefing, specifically as it relates to the Nvidia issue, so we can all get to the bottom of what has happened and what the implications are in terms of America's national security," Jeffries said. The House invited him to a “joint, closed-door briefing” with the heads of the House committees on China, Foreign Affairs, and Intelligence, and that they will focus on his company’s “ security protocols against foreign adversary espionage.” Congress first called the embattled CEO on November 7, a few days after rumors started circulating about Huang’s “closeness” to a particular Chinese executive suspected of passing information to Chinese intelligence. This led to the AI race as we know it today, with the U.S. taking steps to delay China’s advancement for fears that it will use the technology for military purposes. We also don’t know if Huang Le or Alice Huang is actually a Chinese spy or an “innocent” bystander caught in a web of accusations. And, even if she did work with the MSS, the question remains as to whether she specifically targeted the Nvidia CEO or whether Chinese intelligence discovered their indiscretion and used that as a convenient tool for blackmail to extract information from her. However, former CIA agent Darrel Blocker told ABC News that the authorities should just focus on Jensen. “I think that the biggest concern is that the focus or overfocus on just Jensen Huang and Nvidia risks losing sight of the fact that other people have been targeted by the Chinese. Are they talking to the engineers? Are they talking to other people who might have even more access than even the CEO has? So, this focus should not be singular; it should include everyone in the company, and quite frankly, every tech company out there should be looking at all the contacts that their officers and employees have.” “It’s definitely not a one-time thing. When you run a trillion-dollar company, you know that you have a bullseye on your back; whether it’s from competition or rather from nation-states, so this is absolutely not a one-off.
